This is the single source of truth for corpus structure (ADR: OKF rejected as canonical format, 2026-06-19; single canonical representation with no separate authoring layer, 2026-07-09). learningObjectives: Define corruption and its various forms.
Understand the impact of corruption on society.
Identify common examples of corrupt practices.
knowledgeUnits.description: This knowledge unit provides an overview of corruption, its definitions, and its impact on society. It introduces learners to the concept of corruption, its various forms, and the importance of anti-corruption measures.

content.name: What is Corruption?
content.description: An article by the United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC) that provides a comprehensive overview of corruption, its forms, and its impact on society.

sections.title: What is corruption?
sections.markdown:
# Lesson 1 (Section 1): What is corruption?

Corruption is **the abuse of entrusted power for private gain**. Someone is trusted to act for others (a public official, a manager, a committee member) and uses that position to help themselves instead.

> Trust + power + personal gain = corruption

It can happen in government, in business, and in community groups. It is not only about money: favours, jobs and inside information count too.

**Quick check:** a clerk is trusted to process permits fairly. If they speed up a permit for a friend, who loses?

- Other applicants, who wait longer
- The public, who lose faith in fair rules

sections.title: Common forms
sections.markdown:
# Lesson 1 (Section 2): Common forms of corruption

Corruption shows up in a few familiar shapes:

- **Bribery:** offering, giving or accepting something of value to influence an official's decision.
- **Embezzlement:** stealing or misusing money or property you were trusted to look after.
- **Nepotism:** favouring relatives or friends, whatever their qualifications.
- **Conflict of interest:** when your personal interests collide with your duty to the public.

**Example (quick):** an official learns where a new highway will run and buys land there before it is announced. That is a *conflict of interest* built on insider knowledge.

sections.title: Why it matters
sections.markdown:
# Lesson 1 (Section 3): Why it hurts everyone

Corruption is not a victimless shortcut. It:

- **Wastes public money** that should pay for schools, clinics and roads.
- **Weakens fairness**, so people with connections beat people with talent.
- **Erodes trust** in institutions, which makes people less willing to take part.
- **Costs the most to those with the least**, who cannot pay bribes or hire favours.

Spotting it early, and naming it clearly, is the first step to stopping it.

sections.title: Who fights it
sections.markdown:
# Lesson 1 (Section 4): Who helps stop corruption?

A healthy system has several lines of defence:

- **Independent anti-corruption agencies** investigate and prevent corrupt practices *without political interference*.
- **Whistleblowers** expose illegal or unethical practices from the inside, and need protection when they speak up.
- **Transparency and accountability** rules (open records, audits) make hiding wrongdoing harder.
- **Frameworks like the UN Convention against Corruption (UNCAC)** set shared standards countries agree to follow.

Everyone has a part: citizens, businesses and community groups included.

sections.title: Ready to check
sections.markdown:
# Lesson 1 (Section 5): Recap

You now have the core ideas:

- Corruption = **abuse of entrusted power for private gain**.
- Forms: bribery, embezzlement, nepotism, conflicts of interest.
- It drains resources, weakens fairness and erodes trust.
- Agencies, whistleblowers and transparency help stop it.

Want to read more? See the source linked in the lesson panel. When you are ready, continue to the quiz to test what this lesson taught.

questions.questionText: What is the definition of corruption?
options: Abuse of power for personal gain
questions.hint: Think about the misuse of authority for personal benefit.

questions.questionText: Which term describes offering money or gifts to influence the decision of an official?
questions.hint: Consider an illicit payment made under the table to secure a favorable outcome.

questions.questionText: What is nepotism in a workplace or government setting?
options: Favoring relatives or friends regardless of qualifications
questions.hint: It comes from the Latin word for 'nephew' and refers to family bias.

options: Stealing or misappropriating funds entrusted to your care
Refusing to pay annual property taxes
questions.hint: Focus on the violation of trust involving company or public money.

questions.questionText: What is the main purpose of an independent anti-corruption agency?
options: To investigate and prevent corrupt practices without political interference
questions.hint: Their core role is oversight, investigation, and enforcement free from outside control.

questions.questionText: A government official uses insider knowledge to buy property before a highway route is announced. This is an example of what?
questions.hint: It occurs when personal interests collide with an official duty to the public.

questions.questionText: What role does a 'whistleblower' play in combating corruption?
options: Enforcing penalties on behalf of the judiciary
Exposing illegal or unethical practices within an organization
questions.hint: They bring hidden misconduct into the light from the inside.

cards.back: Corruption is the abuse of entrusted power for private gain.
cards.hint: Think about the misuse of power for personal benefit.

cards.back: Bribery is offering, giving, receiving, or soliciting something of value to influence the actions of an official.
cards.hint: It involves something of value exchanged to influence an official's actions.

cards.back: Nepotism is favoritism granted to relatives or friends, often by giving them jobs.
cards.hint: Think of favoritism toward family members or close friends.

cards.back: Embezzlement is the theft or misappropriation of funds placed in one's trust or belonging to one's employer.
cards.hint: It is the misuse or theft of money entrusted to someone.

cards.front: What is the role of an independent anti-corruption agency?
cards.back: Its role is to investigate and prevent corruption without political interference.
cards.hint: Focus on investigating and preventing corruption independently.
